  Ordinance Overview  Purpose
 The ordinance intends to address the environmental and
  human health problems associated with producing and
disposing of single-use plastics and expanded polystyrene.

CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Small Business Assistance Task Force
  Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, March 26, 2024
  3:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  March 26, 2024 / 3:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian Gold, Councilmember Lili Bosse, Deputy City Manager Keith
  Davis, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis, Director of
  Community Development Michael Forbes, Public Works Env Comp & Sust
  Program Manager Josette Descalzo, Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce
  President and CEO Todd Johnson, Chamber Director of Economic
  Development & Government Affairs Brittany Ganson, Chamber of
  Commerce Government Affairs Consultant Ted Green

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Welcome, Introductions and Purpose of the Task Force:
  a. Larry Johnson: Program Lead Advisor at El Camino College Small Business
  Development Center
  b. Mario Landeros: Pioneer Hardware
  c. Barry Axelrod: Beverly Hills Cookies
  d. Tiffany Davis: Key Entertainment
  e. Sherry Andrews: Epiphany Boutique

  3) Ordinance Regulating Single-Use Plastic and Expanded Polystyrene:
  a. Presentation by Josette Descalzo:
  i. The City’s ordinance was modeled on the LA County Ordinance to provide
  consistency between the city and county unincorporated areas.
  ii. Cost increases for affected businesses should be minimal.
  iii. Mobile food facilities will have 1.5 years to implement the ordinance,
  temporary food facilities, the famers market, and catering companies will
  have 2 years to implement. All other affected businesses have one year to
  comply with the ordinance.
  iv. The Key provisions of the ordinance are that:
 Highlights for March 26, 2024
Small Business Assistance Task Force Committee

  1. Food Facilities cannot distribute single-use articles that are neither
  compostable nor recyclable.
  2. Retail establishments cannot sell expanded polystyrene products.
  3. Third-party online food ordering business mut allow food facilities to
  indicate which single- use foodware accessories they offer for
  customer selection.
  4. There is flexibility for certain food applications w/o options for
  compliant products.
  5. Full-service restaurants must provide multiservice utensils instead
  of single use articles to dine in customers.
  v.  The city will host a follow up workshop, send out reminders, provide a
  compliant product resource for businesses to use, and provide technical
  assistance on supplies.
  vi.  The city also has an early adopter incentive program which provides one
  month, or $500, of compliant products for businesses that want to switch
  prior to the one-year deadline.
  vii.  Lined containers for heated products are exempted from the ordinance.
  viii.  The only sizeable difference between the city and county ordinance is that
  the city does not exempt street food vendors like the county does.
  ix.  Shakes are required to use a clear plastic beverage container rated 1,2 or
  5.
  x.  Businesses will have to apply for a waiver, they are not granted
  automatically.

  4) Overview: LAEDC Opportunities for Small Business for Major Upcoming Regions;
  Sports & Entertainment Events:
  a. Presentation by Magdalena Davis:
  i. The Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation is a nonprofit
  focusing solely on economic development.
  ii. LA has several routine sporting events due to our large number of
  professional sports teams.
  iii. There are four major upcoming sporting events: the 2026 World Cup, the
  2026 NBA All Star Game, Super Bowl LXI in 2027, and the 2028 Summer
  Olympics.
  iv. There are also several major infrastructure projects under development
  that will affect the local economy, such as the new metro line.
  v. These events boost city revenues through not only TOT, but also through
  increased patronage at local businesses.
  b. UCLA and USC joining the Big 10 is projected to increase tourism due to games.
  c. The LA Sports Entertainment Commission has streamlined the application to
  license things like the LA 2028 logo.
  d. Each change in TOT requires a ballot initiative. There was a proposition to modify
  TOT so that it would increase during these events and lapse the rest of the year,
  but Mayor Gold stated that it may only be legally able to do the opposite, where
  the base TOT is high, but is lowered whenever there isn’t a major event.
 Highlights for March 26, 2024
Small Business Assistance Task Force Committee

  e. Hotels would also increase their prices so the City will already receive increased
  TOT revenues due to that.

  5) Information Sharing & Discussion by Small Business Task Force:
  a. Sherry Andrews: Business is still slow due to depressed tourism rates, and those
  that come in have less disposable income than they did previously, but foot traffic
  has increased in the past four weeks.
  b. City staff are currently drafting an Ordinance to allow A-frame signs that will be
  sent to the council later this year. This will be brought alongside an ordinance that
  will allow for queuing on the sidewalk.
  c. The strike and October 7th were not good for businesses around Christmas. A
  proposal was made to have a small business group chat to identify suspicious
  individuals as well as a proposal to have a city initiative to shop locally.
  d. Sherry also noticed that tourists have stopped talking about safety and safety
  issues, only locals are.
  e. This section closed off with everyone thanking and congratulating Mayor Gold and
  Councilmember Bosse for their 13 years of service.

  6) Future Agenda Items Discussion:
  a. On April 10 there will be a parking façade community outreach meeting from 4-6
  PM.

  7) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: March 26, 2024 / 4:02 PM
